title: Integral exceptional inverse image along a closed immersion
statement: Work in the standing setting [sk-def-sfb-dc-setting]: fix a prime $\ell$, a field $k$ of characteristic $p>0$ with $p\ne\ell$, and separated finite-type $k$-schemes. Fix a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ with valuation ring $\mathcal O_E$ [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension], regarded as a condensed ring [sk-def-sfb-condensed-ring]. All derived categories use module objects over the pulled-back coefficient ring $\mathcal O_{E,T}$ [sk-def-sfb-module-objects], and $\Dbc$ means bounded constructible complexes [sk-def-sfb-constructible]. Let $i:Z\hookrightarrow X$ be a closed immersion [def-weil-closed-immersion], and let $R\underline\Gamma_Z$ be the derived sections-with-support functor of [det-lem-formal-closed-support-derived]. For $K\in\Dbc(X,\mathcal O_E)$, one has $R\underline\Gamma_ZK\in\Dbc(Z,\mathcal O_E)$ and an isomorphism $i^!K\simeq R\underline\Gamma_ZK$, natural in $K$, where $i^!$ is the integral right adjoint of [det-prop-int-brown-adjoint] on the full localizing categories $\Loc(\Dbc(-,\mathcal O_E))$ [sk-def-localizing-closure].

proof.text: Let $j:U\hookrightarrow X$ be the open complement of $i$. The field $k$ is Noetherian (its only ideals are $0,k$), hence $X$ is Noetherian by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-over-noetherian]. For each affine open $V\subseteq X$, the open subscheme $U\cap V$ is quasi-compact by [lem-weil-pbc-noetherian-open-subscheme-noetherian], applied to the Noetherian scheme $X$. Thus $j$ is quasi-compact. It is of finite type by [lem-weil-pbc-qc-open-immersion-finite-type] and separated by [lem-weil-pbc-separated-cancellation](a). Also $U$ is quasi-compact by [lem-weil-pbc-noetherian-open-subscheme-noetherian]. Write $a_X:X\to\operatorname{Spec}k$ for the structure morphism and equip $U$ with $a_U=a_Xj$. The composite $a_U$ is separated and locally of finite type by [lem-weil-pbc-proper-fp-permanence](e). It is quasi-compact since every affine open of $\operatorname{Spec}k$ is either empty or the whole one-point space, with preimage empty or $U$. Consequently $a_U$ is of finite type by [def-weil-finite-type-morphism], so $U$ is a standing scheme and $j$ a morphism of the setting. The coefficient ring is the pulled-back condensed $\mathcal O_E$, so it is among the admissible coefficient rings in [det-lem-formal-closed-support-sheaves]. In particular its assertion (2) gives exactness of the direct image $i_*$.

source.place: Opening sentence; coefficient-ring scope of the formal support construction

proof.text: The closed immersion $i$ is proper, hence separated of finite type, by [lem-weil-pbc-closed-immersion-proper](a). Use the compactification $c=(Z\xrightarrow{\mathrm{id}_Z}Z\xrightarrow{i}X)$. Its open map is quasi-compact: the preimage of any affine open under the identity is that affine open itself. Apply the current compactification formula in [det-prop-int-brown-construction] to obtain $Ri_!^c=Ri_*D((\mathrm{id}_Z)_!)$. Extension by zero along the identity is the identity on sheaves and its termwise functor $D((\mathrm{id}_Z)_!)$ is therefore the identity on complexes and the derived category. The same cited statement supplies the canonical comparison from the chosen compactification defining $Ri_!$ to $c$, so $Ri_!\simeq Ri_!^c\simeq Ri_*$. Since $i_*$ is exact by step 1, applying it termwise to a quasi-isomorphism preserves cohomology isomorphisms; applying it to the K-injective resolution that computes $Ri_*$ thus gives $Ri_*\simeq i_*$. These natural identifications give $Ri_!\simeq i_*$ on the integral localizing categories.

source.place: Final paragraph: use Ri_!=i_* for a closed immersion

proof.text: Apply [det-lem-formal-closed-support-derived](1),(3) with $\Lambda=\mathcal O_E$. It supplies the natural distinguished triangle $F\to K\to Rj_*j^*K\to F[1]$, with $F=i_*R\underline\Gamma_ZK$, the isomorphism $R\underline\Gamma_ZK\simeq i^*F$, and the natural adjunction $\operatorname{Hom}_X(i_*A,K)\simeq\operatorname{Hom}_Z(A,R\underline\Gamma_ZK)$ on the ambient derived categories. Its sheaf-level hypotheses are precisely the standing scheme and admissible pulled-back coefficients checked in step 1.

source.place: Localization triangle and formal support adjunction

proof.text: Apply [det-lem-int-tensor-pullback](1) to $j:U\to X$, whose source and target are standing schemes by step 1. Thus $J=j^*K\in\Dbc(U,\mathcal O_E)$. The inverse image is the one for the pulled-back condensed coefficient rings; no completed-inverse-image comparison from clause (2) is needed.

source.place: Sentence beginning Its third term lies in Dbc, followed by inverse image

proof.text: Apply [det-thm-sf-pf-adic-open] to $J$ from step 4 and the quasi-compact open immersion $j$ from step 1. Its $k,\ell,E$ are those fixed here, and choose the uniformizer of $E$. Its coefficient sheaf $\mathcal O_{E,T}=p_T^*\underline{\mathcal O_E}$ is the pulled-back condensed ring on $T=U,X$ used here, and its direct image is the same derived module direct image. Hence $C=Rj_*J\in\Dbc(X,\mathcal O_E)$.

source.place: Sentence beginning Its third term lies in Dbc, followed by inverse image

proof.text: Clause (1) of [det-lem-int-integral-heart-triangulated] applies with our $k,\ell,X,E$ and the chosen uniformizer: its $R_X=p_X^*\underline{\mathcal O_E}$ is our coefficient ring, so its full triangulated subcategory is our $\Dbc(X,\mathcal O_E)$. Put $F=i_*R\underline\Gamma_ZK$ as in step 3. In the triangle $F\to K\to C\to F[1]$, reverse rotation (TR2 of [def-weil-triangulated-category]) gives $C[-1]\to F\to K\to C$. By [def-weil-triangulated-subcategory], $C[-1]$ belongs to the subcategory because $C$ does, and the two-endpoint condition then puts $F$ in it because $K$ does. Thus $F\in\Dbc(X,\mathcal O_E)$.

source.place: Sentence beginning Its third term lies in Dbc, followed by inverse image

proof.text: Apply [det-lem-int-tensor-pullback](1) to $i:Z\to X$ and $F$ from step 6. Both schemes are standing schemes, so $i^*F\in\Dbc(Z,\mathcal O_E)$. The fiber formula [det-lem-formal-closed-support-derived](3), used in step 3, identifies $R\underline\Gamma_ZK$ with $i^*F$. Constructibility and boundedness are invariant under isomorphism by their definition [sk-def-sfb-constructible]. Therefore $R\underline\Gamma_ZK\in\Dbc(Z,\mathcal O_E)$.

source.place: Sentence beginning Its third term lies in Dbc, followed by inverse image

proof.text: Put $B=i^!K$ and $H=R\underline\Gamma_ZK$, and write $\mathcal T_T=\Loc(\Dbc(T,\mathcal O_E))$. Apply the current [det-prop-int-brown-adjoint] to $f=i$: the standing separated finite-type schemes and pulled-back condensed coefficients are those of the statement, and step 2 verifies the morphism hypothesis. Its $Ri_!$ is defined using the chosen compactification and the same module-object convention as step 2, so the natural identification $Ri_!\simeq i_*$ applies to this very left adjoint. By [det-def-localizing-closure-ctf-equals-bc](2), applied to the standing (hence qcqs) schemes $Z,X$ and $\Lambda=\mathcal O_E$, one has $\Dctf(-,\mathcal O_E)=\Dbc(-,\mathcal O_E)$ and $\Loc(\Dctf(-,\mathcal O_E))=\Loc(\Dbc(-,\mathcal O_E))$; these are the equalities under which the Brown statement is formulated, and they identify the constructible generators with those of [sk-def-localizing-closure]. Thus $K\in\mathcal T_X$, $H\in\mathcal T_Z$ by step 7, and $B\in\mathcal T_Z$ by the Brown right adjoint's stated codomain. For every $A\in\mathcal T_Z$, the explicitly stated natural Brown bijection $\operatorname{Hom}(Ri_!A,K)\simeq\operatorname{Hom}(A,i^!K)$, inverted and composed with step 2 and [det-lem-formal-closed-support-derived](1), gives $\Phi_A:\operatorname{Hom}(A,B)\simeq\operatorname{Hom}(i_*A,K)\simeq\operatorname{Hom}(A,H)$, natural in $A$ and $K$. Fullness in [sk-def-localizing-closure] identifies these Hom sets with the ambient derived Hom sets. Only the given adjunction and its naturality are used; no unqualified uniqueness assertion or preservation of the whole localizing category by the ambient support functor is required.

source.place: Yoneda paragraph: the two natural Hom identifications

proof.text: Write $\alpha_K=\Phi_B(1_B):B\to H$ and $\beta_K=\Phi_H^{-1}(1_H):H\to B$. Naturality in $A$ says $\Phi_A(g)=\alpha_Kg$. Consequently $\alpha_K\beta_K=1_H$; injectivity of $\Phi_B$ then gives $\beta_K\alpha_K=1_B$, since both sides map to $\alpha_K$. For a map $u:K\to L$, naturality of $\Phi$ in $K$, evaluated at $1_{i^!K}$, gives $(R\underline\Gamma_Zu)\alpha_K=\alpha_L(i^!u)$. Thus the $\alpha_K$ form the required natural isomorphism.

source.place: Last sentence: explicit Yoneda inverse and naturality

proof_origin.place: Localization, integral constructibility, and counit Hom comparison; last sentence expanded explicitly
